text: Nebulas are enormous clouds of gas and dust in space, often visible as glowing regions of light in the night sky. These vast structures can be tens of thousands of light-years across and contain millions of suns. Observing nebulas through a telescope reveals intricate details such as glowing regions, dust lanes, and intricate patterns that are only visible in space. Astronomers use telescopes to study nebulas because they provide an unparalleled view of the cosmos, revealing the raw materials from which stars are born. Telescopic analysis of nebulas helps scientists understand the evolution of galaxies and the formation of new stars.
